text:
anya: quick heads-up — after the recent SDK change that toggles streaming clients to send `Cache-Control: no-cache` we see a measurable drop in prefix cache hit-rate. On a representative chat workload: hit-rate went from 62% -> 54% and p50 latency +30ms. Can we triage?

kevin: ack, saw the alert. change was to reduce stale streaming responses; the SDK sets `no-cache` only for chunked streaming replies. Thought it would be harmless for prefix caching.

samir: do we have a profiler snapshot that ties misses to warmup behavior vs keying differences?

maria: throwing the quick numbers I pulled:
```
qps: 420
prefix_hits_before: 62.1
prefix_hits_after: 54.0
kv_warmup_time_median: 12ms -> 28ms
avg_tokens_per_request: 48 -> 39
```
Looks like warmup is suffering — more short-lived streams + explicit no-cache -> fewer prefix reuse.

ryan: kernel/batching angle: when average seq len drops the runtime picked a different kernel path in about 18% of requests (fallback to fallback-kernel-int8 in our traces) which has worse throughput for those batch sizes. That can amplify latencies when KV cache isn't helping.

anya: interesting. So it's a twofold regression: clients stop allowing prefix caching (header) and our runtime shifts kernels due to shorter sequences. Either alone might be OK, together is painful.

kevin: on SDK side we can make cache header opt-in instead of blanket `no-cache`. Proposal: add `X-RW-PREFIX-CACHE: {auto|opt-in|opt-out}` and default streaming to `auto` which keeps previous behavior unless user opts out.

maria: +1 but watch retries: we observed retry storms where client retries on upstream 502 and the retried request is sent with `no-cache` (different SDK path) and kills hit-rate during failover windows. That explains some spike patterns in the timeline.

samir: reproducible script? if we can replay stream/open/close patterns with the SDK we can measure improvements. Anyone has a small repro?

sdk-bot: replay harness available at `internal/sdk/playback/stream-replay` — can run with `--simulate-retries` and `--vary-chunking`.

kevin: I ran a quick ablation: switching streaming default to `auto` (server treats `auto` like allow-if-prefix-present) recovers ~6% of hits in the same window. But we need an A/B and a server-side fallback because some older clients will keep sending `no-cache`.

ryan: server-side heuristic idea: if request has `X-RW-STREAMING: 1` and body contains a prompt prefix tokenization fingerprint (we can compute cheap hash on first 128B) — treat as cacheable unless explicit `no-cache`. That preserves safety while keeping existing clients supported.

anya: is that safe for PII/regulatory customers? We can't cache sensitive prefixes. Need KMS/tenant rules check.

maria: for Private/Dedicated teams we must honor per-tenant policy. But for hosted public customers we can add an allowlist. Also add instrumentation flag `cache.heuristic=true` to measure false-positive risk.

samir: warmup strategy: consider proactive KV warmup on route resolution if we see repeated short sequences from the same session_id. Basically prefetch probable next-prefixes into GPU cache once we detect a pattern. Profiling shows prefetch reduces median warmup from 28ms -> 9ms in a trial.

kevin: prefetch is good but increases write/evict churn. Need to tune eviction window and prefetch budget by model and tenant tier. Optimize per-model sequence distribution.

ryan: also look at batching heuristics: if we detect many short requests (<64 tokens) within 50ms window we should slightly increase batch wait (to 20-30ms) for better kernel utilization, but that trades p50 latency. Might be fine for non-interactive workloads.

anya: concrete action items: 
- kevin: implement `X-RW-PREFIX-CACHE` header in SDK with default `auto` and add opt-in flag `enablePrefixCacheForStreaming` in SDK config.
- eng-runtime (ryan/samir): add server-side heuristic: treat `auto` as cacheable if prefix fingerprint matches allowlist and emit `cache.heuristic` metric.
- eng-runtime (samir): run prefetch pilot for chat route and measure warmup reduction.
- infra/sre: run short A/B with rollback window and watch 502-related retry cascade.

maria: one more edge case — streaming + streaming-resume retry: resumed streams append tokens and produce different cache keys because timestamp/nonce is in key. We should canonicalize prefix keying to ignore ephemeral sdk-nonces so retries/warmup see same key.

kevin: good catch — SDK will stop sending ephemeral `client-stream-id` in the cache-key header and instead include it in `X-RW-TRACE` only.

sre-bot: incident created: INC-2026-174999 — assigned to eng-runtime and sdk. Monitoring thresholds updated: prefix_hit_rate < 56% triggers page.

anya: thanks all. I'll follow-up with a short RFC summarizing header design + server heuristic + prefetch pilot. Keep thread updated with the A/B results. :thumbsup:
